outcome: The general conjecture remains open; work since January 2024 consists of survey/strategy papers and technical tools within the Borovik/Hrushovski program, plus resolutions of a distinct, differently-named conjecture (Borovik-Cherlin) that shares an author's name but is not a case of the Cherlin-Zilber algebraicity conjecture.
summary: The Cherlin-Zilber (algebraicity) conjecture — every infinite simple group of finite Morley rank is a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field — remains open, and I found no result since 26 January 2024 that settles the general conjecture, settles a new case (rank, type, or class) of it, or moves a bound on it. The current Wikipedia article's most recent cited progress is Altinel-Borovik-Cherlin (2008) plus Frécon's elimination of Morley-rank-3 bad groups, which appeared in JAMS in 2018 (arXiv work from 2016-2017) — well before the frozen revision, so it is not a window event. Since January 2024 I found: (1) Berkman & Borovik, 'Groups acting generically multiply transitively...' and related affine-type papers (arXiv:2405.07307, May-Dec 2024) which are structural lemmas in the Borovik classification program, not case settlements; (2) Kowalski & Uğurlu Kowalski, 'On generic and supertight automorphisms' (arXiv:2604.20415, April 2026), giving partial evidence for a Hrushovski-suggested principle ('fixed points are pseudofinite') used in the classification strategy, explicitly not a resolution; (3) Berkman & Borovik, 'The Şiş Kebap Theorem: A Generic Identification Theorem for Groups of Finite Morley Rank' (arXiv:2608.01161, August 2026), a conditional identification theorem (Theorem 1.2, under Prüfer-rank and torus-structure hypotheses A-C) intended as 'Step 6' of a six-step strategy in the Hrushovski Programme — a technical tool, not an unconditional case settlement, since its hypotheses are themselves open problems in the program; and (4) Katrin Tent's 'From the Cherlin-Zilber Conjecture via sharply 2-transitive groups to the Burnside problem' (arXiv:2606.18207, June 2026, to appear in ICM 2026 proceedings), an explicit survey that states no new result and instead discusses sharply-2-transitive groups as a potential source of counterexamples. Separately, I found a cluster of papers proving the 'Borovik-Cherlin conjecture' (arXiv:2106.02537, 2021/2025; arXiv:2609.02198, September 2026) — but per arXiv:2106.02537 and the Berkman-Borovik generic-transitivity literature, this is a distinct conjecture about generic multiple-transitivity bounds for definable homogeneous spaces (k ≤ RM(S)+2, and characterizing generically (n+2)-transitive actions as PGL_{n+1}), applicable across stable theories including ACF₀, differentially closed fields, and compact complex manifolds — not a restriction of the Cherlin-Zilber algebraicity statement about simple groups of finite Morley rank. It shares Cherlin's name (and, in the finite-Morley-rank case, overlapping authors and techniques) but is a different question under §3.1's related-problem/case-of-the-problem test, so its resolutions in ACF₀/CCM (2025) and now arbitrary characteristic (Karhumäki & Ramsey, arXiv:2609.02198, September 2026) do not count as progress on the bullet as stated. No AI system appears anywhere in this literature: none of the papers I opened mention AI, LLM, or machine-learning assistance, and broader searches for AI-assisted work touching finite-Morley-rank group theory turned up nothing intersecting this conjecture. I am satisfied this is a genuine 'no change' rather than a gap in my search: I checked the current Wikipedia article, the most recent arXiv listings under math.GR and math.LO citing Cherlin-Zilber or algebraicity conjecture, the 2026 ICM survey (which is itself a comprehensive contemporary account with no new result), and cross-checked the namesake conjecture that could plausibly be miscounted as a case.
competing_reading: Someone building the numerator from titles or acknowledgements alone could easily miscount the Borovik-Cherlin conjecture's 2025-2026 resolutions (arXiv:2106.02537's ACF₀/CCM cases and arXiv:2609.02198's extension to arbitrary characteristic) as progress on Cherlin-Zilber, since both share Cherlin as a co-namesake and both concern finite-Morley-rank-adjacent stable-theoretic structures. Under a looser scope reading where any theorem invoking 'finite Morley rank' groups counts, the Şiş Kebap Theorem (arXiv:2608.01161) might also be read as 'partial' progress rather than a conditional tool, since it does unconditionally identify a restricted class of groups as Chevalley groups under stated hypotheses A-C. I judge these hypotheses are themselves unresolved parts of the classification program (making the result a strategic lemma, not a case settlement of the conjecture as stated), but a reader who considers 'discharging one lemma toward a six-step program' sufficient for `partial` status could reasonably disagree.
what_would_settle_it: A precise reading (or a co-author's clarification) of whether Theorem 1.2 of arXiv:2608.01161 applies unconditionally to a nonempty class of previously-unclassified simple groups of finite Morley rank (which would make it `partial`), versus applying only under hypotheses that are themselves still open (making it a conditional tool, as I've classified it); and confirmation from a model theorist that the Borovik-Cherlin conjecture is formally understood as conceptually distinct from, rather than a special case of, the Cherlin-Zilber algebraicity conjecture.
